name: SET domain containing 1A, histone lysine methyltransferase

function.text: SETD1A encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD1A. Annotated molecular activities include histone H3K4 methyltransferase activity and histone H3K4 monomethyltransferase activity. It participates in regulation of chromatin organization and brain development.

germline.text: Strong or definitive GenCC assertions link constitutional variants to neurodevelopmental disorder with speech impairment and dysmorphic facies (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: This gene is included in cancer-panel definitions, but a disease-specific somatic association has not been assigned from the alteration-context sources reviewed for this draft.

germline_associations.mechanism: Autosomal dominant; strong GenCC assertion from Labcorp Genetics (formerly Invitae). Allele-specific mechanism requires review.

function.text: SETD1A encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD1A. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4) via a non-processive mechanism. It forms part of chromatin remodeling machinery, forms H3K4me1, H3K4me2 and H3K4me3 methylation marks at active chromatin sites where transcription and DNA repair take place. It is required for H3K4me1 mark at stalled replication forks.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with neurodevelopmental disorder with speech impairment and dysmorphic facies (autosomal dominant).
